target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs a full sorted clone of all task records and a full scan of in-process generated-media activity. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless
- ClawSweeper confirmed the shape: "one canonical bulk pending-generated-media session-key snapshot that combines active in-process work with nonterminal persisted requester and owner keys"

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6: `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` covers empty set, in-process activity, requesterSessionKey, ownerKey, terminal exclusion, non-generated-media exclusion, combined snapshot)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass (mock updated to use `buildPendingSet`; two pending-media tests now verify correct sessionKey membership)
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +136 −5 lines
  - `src/tasks/generated-media-task-activity.ts` — new `getAllActiveGeneratedMediaSessionKeys` export
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.ts` — new `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` helper
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — one snapshot call before the loop, `Set.has()` per row
  - `src/tasks/task-status-access.test.ts` — 6 new tests
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — mock updated for new function
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `listTaskRecords`, `getActiveGeneratedMediaTasks`, `isTerminalTaskStatus`
- **Live proof:** standalone simulation at realistic scale (direct `node --import tsx`):

```
=== Session Reaper Batch Snapshot — Proof ===

[Case 1] Correctness — old and new produce identical results
  old: 50 pending (0.7ms, 50 listTaskRecords calls)
  new: 50 pending (0.4ms, 1 listTaskRecords call)
  ✓ identical results for all 50 sessions
  ✓ pending key sets match exactly

[Case 2] Performance scaling — O(S×T) vs O(T+S)
  scale: 500 sessions × 1000 tasks
  old: 13.6ms — 500 full task-list scans (clone+sort each)
  new: 0.5ms — 1 full task-list scan + 500 Set.has() lookups
  speedup: 27.2x
  ✓ identical results at scale (500 × 1000)
  ✓ old: 500 listTaskRecords calls
  ✓ new approach is faster
  real clone cost: old=500,000 element copies
  real clone cost: new=1,000 element copies

[Case 3] requesterSessionKey + ownerKey contract preserved
  pending: [owner-x, req-a, req-b]
  ✓ requesterSessionKey captured
  ✓ ownerKey captured (different from requester)
  ✓ requester == owner still captured
  ✓ chat task excluded (non-generated-media)
  ✓ terminal task excluded
  ✓ all 5 session keys match

[Case 4] Empty world — snapshot is empty set
  ✓ empty when no tasks or active media

[Case 5] Worst-case — every session has continuation, none have pending media
  1000 sessions, every one has continuation but 0 have pending media
  old: 0.4ms (1000 listTaskRecords calls)
  new: 0.2ms (1 listTaskRecords call, snap size=1)
  ✓ all 1000 sessions match
  ✓ old path: 1000 listTaskRecords calls
  speedup: 2.0x

=== Results: 18 passed / 0 failed ===
```

- In the real `listTaskRecords`, each call also performs a `toSorted(compareTasksNewestFirst)` — the old path does 500 sorts, the new path does 1. The simulation captures the essential O(S×T) → O(T+S) transition; real-world speedup is larger at scale.
- **Performance:** sweep goes from O(S × (T + M)) to O(T + M + S) where S = session rows, T = persisted tasks, M = active in-process media entries
